item.title: 5 Free Microsoft GitHub Courses to Learn Data Science and Artificial Intelligence
item.description:
# 5 Free Microsoft GitHub Courses to Learn Data Science and Artificial Intelligence Explore five free Microsoft GitHub courses covering data science, machine learning, artificial intelligence, generative AI, LLMs, RAG, fine-tuning, and AI agents.
## 3. Artificial Intelligence for Beginners Microsoft's **[Artificial Intelligence for Beginners](https://github.com/microsoft/AI-For-Beginners)** expands on machine learning and introduces the broader foundations of artificial intelligence.
You will also explore technologies and techniques such as **[PyTorch](https://pytorch.org/)**, **[TensorFlow](https://www.tensorflow.org/)**, convolutional neural networks, recurrent neural networks, embeddings, transformers, transfer learning, autoencoders, and generative adversarial networks.

item.title: Bipartisan, big tech push for AI regulation comes as Trump claims 'hoax'
item.description:
## Google DeepMind researcher steps down, warning AI has potential to 'kill us all' Bilal Chughtai, who resigned from the [Google-owned AI lab](https://www.foxnews.com/category/tech/artificial-intelligence) in July 2026 after working on AGI safety and alignment, said "we might be running out of time to avoid" the threat of being killed by AI.
## Antony Blinken says AI has potential for 'extraordinary good' and 'catastrophic consequences' Secretary of State Antony Blinken said [AI has the potential](https://www.foxnews.com/category/tech/artificial-intelligence) for "extraordinary good, but also for catastrophic consequences" if its development outpaces human ability to put necessary guardrails in place.
## Kamala Harris’ past AI remarks resurface as debate over safeguards intensifies Former Vice President Kamala Harris’ past explanation of [artificial intelligence](https://www.foxnews.com/category/tech/artificial-intelligence) resurfaced after she joined growing calls to slow the development of advanced AI systems.
It means artificial intelligence,” Harris said before explaining that AI involves machines learning from the information they receive.
## Pentagon fires back at AI ‘doomers,’ vows US will remain dominant The new frontier of artificial intelligence belongs to us, not doomers.
The Pentagon’s technology office pushed back against calls to slow artificial intelligence development, declaring that the United States will control the technology’s next chapter.
“The new frontier of artificial intelligence belongs to us, not doomers,” the Department of War CTO wrote on X.

item.title: Trump Says a Smart President Is All That’s Needed to Rein In A.I.
Why Steve Bannon sided with Sanders, not Trump, on AI
Johnson plays down AI warnings : ‘You’re not all going to be dead in 10 years’
item.description:
### Inside Congress newsletter Speaker Mike Johnson dismissed fears of civilizational wipeout from artificial intelligence, comparing the recent alarms from inside AI labs to what he characterized as overblown warnings on the political left over climate change.
## [Rebel Democrats again help House GOP advance floor agenda](https://www.politico.com/news/2026/09/15/golden-gluesenkamp-perez-rule-vote-01078189) Two Senate Republicans said Tuesday that providing antitrust exemptions to artificial intelligence companies to facilitate discussions on how to make AI safer should be taken off the table — as lawmakers discuss ways to respond to industry warnings about the need for guardrails on the rapidly evolving technology.
Sen. [Bernie Sanders](https://directory.politicopro.com/congress/member/60c3186f-cbc6-4a13-90b4-7c3cb5e0567c) decried Washington on Tuesday for failing to regulate artificial intelligence, including the advanced models that AI researchers, tech executives and safety advocates warn pose an existential risk to humanity.
Josh Gottheimer said proposals to use third-party organizations to evaluate the safety of frontier artificial intelligence models are not enough, instead endorsing a mandatory government vetting regime.
The Republican cosponsor of bipartisan artificial intelligence safety legislation said he sat down with OpenAI’s top lobbyist a day before the company backed a key provision in the bill that’s struggled to gain traction on Capitol Hill.
He did not address the topic that has dominated conversations in Congress in recent days: the risk posed by artificial intelligence and what, if anything, lawmakers ought to do about it.
